content: This medication should be discarded properly when it is expired or no longer needed. The information provided here was last revised in July 2024. Important Usage Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Warning: Estrogens, whether used alone or in combination with another hormone (progestin), have been associated with rare but serious side effects. Discuss the risks and benefits of hormone therapy with your doctor. Estrogens can increase the risk of uterine cancer (endometrial cancer). Taking a progestin as directed by your doctor can help reduce this risk. In postmenopausal women, estrogens, with or without a progestin, may increase the risk of breast or ovarian cancer, stroke, dementia, and serious blood clots. The likelihood of these serious side effects may depend on the dose of estrogen and the duration of use. This medication should be used at the lowest effective dose and for the shortest duration necessary. Regularly discuss the use of this medication with your doctor and have periodic check-ups (e.g., every 3 to 6 months) to determine if continued use is necessary. If long-term use is required, you should undergo regular comprehensive physical exams (e.g., annually) as directed by your doctor. Uses: This medication is a hormone used by women to alleviate vaginal symptoms of menopause, such as dryness, burning, and itching. These symptoms occur due to decreased estrogen production in the body. When treating only vaginal symptoms of menopause, products applied directly inside the vagina (such as this medication) should be considered first. How to Use: Before starting this medication and each time you get a refill, read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Use the medication exactly as directed by your doctor. Fill the applicator with the medication according to the instructions, insert it high into the vagina, and press the plunger to release the medication. After use, clean the applicator with warm soapy water and rinse thoroughly. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Follow your dosing schedule carefully. Possible Side Effects: Nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or weight changes may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause serious (sometimes fatal) problems due to blood clots, such as heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. Severe allergic reactions to this product are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Avoid smoking or using tobacco. Inform your doctor if you have recently undergone or will undergo surgery, or if you will be confined to a chair or bed for an extended period (e.g., during a long plane flight), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots, especially when using estrogen products. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on your face and skin (melasma). Sunlight may worsen this effect, so limit your time in the sun and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. Some estrogen products contain mineral oil, which can weaken rubber products such as latex condoms, cervical caps, and diaphragms, potentially leading to their failure. Consult your pharmacist if you are unsure whether your product contains mineral oil. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It passes into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., metyrapone test), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Monitoring and Lifestyle Recommendations: While using this medication, regular comprehensive physical exams, including lab and/or medical tests (e.g., blood pressure, breast exam/mammogram, pelvic exam, Pap smear), should be conducted. Follow your doctor’s instructions for breast self-examinations and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Preventing or managing high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes can reduce your risk of heart disease and stroke. Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat/low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help control or prevent these conditions. Engage in mental exercises (e.g., reading, solving crossword puzzles) to help prevent dementia. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
